record.original_question: Find a number that has a square root and remains a square after adding 10 dirhams and also after subtracting 10 dirhams.

evidence.quote: Problem 18 Find a number that admits a square root such that, if you add ten dirhams to it, the result admits a square root, and if you subtract ten dirhams, the result also admits a square root.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Determine whether there exists a positive rational number $x$ such that all three of $x$, $x+10$, and $x-10$ are squares of rational numbers. Equivalently, decide whether $10$ is a congruent number in the following sense: does there exist a rational number $y>0$ such that both $y^{2}+10$ and $y^{2}-10$ are squares of rational numbers? If such a number exists, exhibit one explicitly; if not, prove that no such number exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is the classical congruum/congruent-number question for n = 10. The set of congruent numbers is well studied; 10 is not on the list of congruent numbers (the congruent numbers up to 20 are 5, 6, 7, 13, 14, 15, 20). Since 10 = 2·5 with 2 not a square, and 10 fails Tunnell's criterion (and equivalently the associated elliptic curve y² = x³ − 100x has rank 0), no rational number x satisfies the three simultaneous square conditions. The problem is therefore considered solved (no solution exists).

status_evidence.title: Congruent number - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The sequence of (squarefree) congruent numbers starts 5, 6, 7, 13, 14, 15, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 28, 29, 30, 31, ...
status_evidence.claim: 10 is not in the list of congruent numbers, so no rational y with y²±10 both rational squares exists.

status_evidence.title: OEIS A003273 (Congruent numbers)
status_evidence.claim: 10 is absent from the OEIS list of congruent numbers.
